- If sentiment shows strong bullish (e.g., +1.00) in recent days, model tends to overestimate and overshoot — reduce forecast slope slightly.
- If sentiment shows strong bearish (e.g., -1.00) in recent days, model tends to underestimate — increase forecast slightly to avoid underreaction.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overreacts and continues upward — cap forecast growth to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (e.g., 0.00 or 0.25), model often fails to capture mean reversion — adjust forecast to align with recent 5–10 day average.
- If true outcome shows strong divergence from model in first 5–7 days of forecast horizon, model is lagging — increase initial forecast by 1–2% to catch early momentum.
- If sentiment history includes multiple +1.00 or -1.00 entries, model tends to overfit sentiment — apply smoothing or dampen sentiment-driven adjustments by 30–50%.
